page: Amazon Web Services x2idn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro hypervisor instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz, delivering 32 physical cores and 64 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Compute capabilities include hardware instruction support for AVX-512, AES cryptography, and BMI2. Memory capacity is substantial, providing 1024 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, establishing a high 16:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio suited for stateful and memory-bound systems.

The instance integrates 1900 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 50 Gbps baseline network interface. There are no discrete hardware accelerators included. In benchmark testing, the x2idn.16xlarge achieves top-quartile results in PassMark database operations (26,134.77) and overall PassMark CPU scores (56,725.09). It demonstrates strong throughput in static web serving at 46.18 GB/sec and software compilation with Clang (40,360.0). Text generation across large language model benchmarks also registers in the upper 25%, while general stress-ng CPU tasks and cached memory bandwidth show middle-tier performance relative to similar-class architectures.

With 1 TB of RAM and bundled NVMe instance storage, this profile prioritizes extreme memory footprint over raw compute density. The reliance on DDR4 rather than DDR5 caps maximum memory bandwidth, though uncached large-block reads still attain 166.56 GB/sec. Organizations running large in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, Aerospike, or distributed Redis clusters benefit from the consolidated memory density without needing to deploy multiple smaller nodes. It is equally appropriate for high-throughput relational databases, real-time analytics pipelines, and large-scale ETL processing requiring extensive scratchpad SSD space.
description: Amazon Web Services x2idn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server driven by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. Equipped with an Intel Xeon 8375C processor at 3.5 GHz, it supplies 32 physical cores, 64 dedicated vCPUs, and a massive 1024 GB of DDR4 system memory. Complementing its 16:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio are 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 50 Gbps baseline networking, without bundled discrete GPUs. Benchmark results emphasize its strength in data-heavy tasks, showing top-tier performance in database operations, cryptographic execution, software compilation, and static web serving throughput reaching 46.18 GB/sec. The configuration presents an efficient consolidation platform for memory-constrained applications, trading ultra-high single-thread burst performance for immense memory capacity and dedicated multi-core throughput. It is specifically suited for hosting large-scale in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, caching clusters, and data-intensive ETL processing pipelines.
